- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after recent spikes.  
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model should not overcorrect upward — expect mean reversion toward lower range.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >75), model should reduce forecast slope for next 5–7 days to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- When bullish events outnumber bearish (net negative supply), model should not assume sustained high — expect volatility decay and downward correction.  
- If sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid false momentum bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp drop after spike, model should adjust downward by 5–10% in first 5 days to reflect sentiment lag.  
- When supply events are frequent (≥20 events/30d), model should not overfit to recent highs — expect volatility and mean reversion within 10–15 days.
